quote_json: "the direct base class does not have an accessible parameterless instance constructor, a compile-time error"
notes: 1st ed 17.10.4 says the automatically provided default constructor 'simply invokes the parameterless constructor of the direct base class' and that if the direct base class 'does not have an accessible parameterless instance constructor, a compile-time error occurs' (PDF p. 278 lines 52-55). Root(params int[]) is not parameterless: a parameter array is a formal parameter (PDF p. 247 lines 36-38), and the edition uses 'parameterless' only for zero formal parameters, set against 'parameterized' (PDF p. 104 lines 14, 36-38; PDF p. 288 lines 45-46). The note that the default constructor is 'always of the form ... base()' (PDF p. 278 lines 56-57; PDF p. 279 lines 1-4) is informative (PDF p. 27 lines 16-20), and 17.10.1's implicit base() (PDF p. 276 lines 13-20, 27-28) selects a constructor but does not cancel 17.10.4's added error, which only the 7th edition replaces with 'as if ... base()' plus a unique-best rule (PDF p. 482; PDF p. 483 lines 3-4). The witness's explicit 'public Branch() : base() { }' compiles under 1st-ed 14.4.2.1's empty expanded form (PDF p. 149 lines 24-35), so the test isolates automatic-default status. Positive witnesses establish prerequisites; failing originals do not prove mutation sensitivity.

quote_json: "the same declared accessibility."
notes: 17.5.4 (PDF p. 252, lines 18 and 23-24) makes it a compile-time error unless the override and the overridden base method have the same declared accessibility, with no assembly exception, and lines 15-17 expressly locate a protected internal base method declared in another program. Declared accessibility is fixed by the declaration's modifiers (10.5.1, PDF p. 88, lines 5-16), so a protected internal override of a protected internal method keeps the same declared accessibility, and the 1st edition requires acceptance. The rule that a protected internal base from another assembly must be overridden as protected first appears in the 7th edition's 15.6.5 (PDF p. 436). The base is compiled separately, the program is otherwise trivial, and the public mutant is rightly rejected at both levels. Positive witnesses establish prerequisites; failing originals do not prove mutation sensitivity.

quote_json: "same accessibility modifiers, type, and name as"
notes: 17.6.3 (PDF p. 262, lines 23-24) requires an overriding property declaration to specify the exact same accessibility modifiers, type and name as the inherited property, and lines 30-32 apply 17.5.4's override rules to its accessors, with no assembly exception. The override repeats the base's own modifiers, protected internal, which is exactly what the 1st edition requires. Declared accessibility comes from those modifiers (10.5.1, PDF p. 88, lines 5-16), not from the access the importing assembly is left with. The different-assembly 'shall be protected' exception is new in the 7th edition's 15.7.6 (PDF p. 459). Positive witnesses establish prerequisites; failing originals do not prove mutation sensitivity.
